His aunt was a formidable woman, imperious in manner and parsimonious with praise, who kept a ledger of every kindness she had ever done and expected each one to be repaid with interest. She lived in a crenellated house on the hill, surrounded by topiary peacocks and an ornamental moat that had long since silted up. The villagers regarded her with a mixture of awe and exasperation. When the vicar, an ingenuous young man fresh from the seminary, proposed a fete on her lawn, she received him with such glacial courtesy that he left convinced he had committed some unpardonable solecism, though he could never say exactly what it was. The laboratory smelled of solder and burnt coffee. Priya adjusted the oscilloscope, watched the waveform settle into a tremulous sine, and allowed herself a small, sardonic smile. Three months of recalcitrant hardware, of intermittent faults that vanished whenever anyone came to look, and now the circuit behaved with an almost obsequious punctuality. She did not trust it. Experience had taught her that a system which worked the first time was merely waiting for a demonstration in front of the funding committee before it failed in some new and ingenious way. She wrote everything down, photographed the bench, and went home before the luck could change. On the third day the fog lifted and the archipelago appeared, a scattering of green islands on a pewter sea. The captain, a phlegmatic Scot who had sailed these waters for thirty years, pointed out the reefs with the stem of his pipe and named each island as if introducing old acquaintances. Gulls wheeled above the mast, raucous and insatiable. The passengers, emboldened by the sunshine, emerged from their cabins pale and blinking, like creatures released from hibernation, and lined the rail to watch a pod of dolphins cavort in the bow wave. Even the curmudgeonly professor, who had complained about everything since they left port, was seen to smile. The expedition reached the escarpment at dusk, and the cartographer, a taciturn woman with an encyclopaedic memory for coastlines, unrolled her vellum maps beside the fire. Nobody spoke.
